# Tokenization Systems

> Independent research, advisory, and infrastructure practice on digital money, tokenization, and tokenomics. Nine SSRN working papers and twenty-two federal comment letters across the GENIUS Act and related dockets, the first eight filed across a 10-day window in April 2026. Run by Zach Zukowski (six years as Senior Investment Analyst at Borderless Capital).

Site: https://tokenization.systems
Contact: zach@tokenization.systems

## About

- [About Tokenization Systems](https://tokenization.systems/about/): what the practice is, what it publishes, who runs it, how to cite it, and the licence terms.

## Research

- [All research](https://tokenization.systems/research/): Nine-paper program across Track A (stablecoins, gateways, settlement infrastructure) and Track B (tokenomics, DePIN, protocol-network governance).
- [Routing the Dollar](https://tokenization.systems/papers/routing-the-dollar/): Stablecoin stress performance varies by gateway, not by token. Three descriptive findings from on-chain data, February 2023 through January 2026. Prepared for FRBNY's Fifth Conference on International Roles of the U.S. Dollar (June 2026).
- [Minimum Viable Equivalence Pack (MVEP)](https://tokenization.systems/papers/mvep/): Ten-category committee checklist testing whether a tokenized product maintains equivalence under stress. Reverse-engineered from the SVB weekend.
- [Who Controls Agentic Payments?](https://tokenization.systems/papers/who-controls-agentic-payments/): First control-layer measurement of agentic payments across x402 on Base, Solana, and Polygon; facilitator concentration clears merger-guidelines thresholds on every chain, and the count layer and value layer have different monopolists.
- [Governance Concentration Beyond Token Allocation](https://tokenization.systems/papers/governance-concentration/): Published in Frontiers in Blockchain (Blockchain Economics, August 2026; 9:1853465, doi 10.3389/fbloc.2026.1853465). Also on SSRN (6599278).
- [Three Tokenization Strategies](https://tokenization.systems/papers/three-strategies/): Institutional tokenization is proceeding through three distinct strategies; Securitize is transfer agent in all three.

## Frameworks

- [Frameworks](https://tokenization.systems/frameworks/): Diligence frameworks the program publishes.
- Control Layer Intensity Index (CLII): five-dimension regulatory-posture score for stablecoin gateways.
- Minimum Viable Equivalence Pack (MVEP): ten-category diligence framework for institutional tokenization.
- MVEP-AI: ten-category framework adapted for AI-operator diligence (composed-product, foundation-model, agentic systems).
- CLII-AI: five-dimension regulatory-posture score for AI operators (Tier 1/2/3 placement).
- FQPSI / PPSI: federal payment-stablecoin issuer diligence frameworks.

## Federal comment letters

- [All letters](https://tokenization.systems/letters/): Twenty-two federal comment letters across seventeen dockets to nine federal agencies, from the GENIUS Act implementation cycle and the SEC draft strategic plan to the CFTC clearing-organization collection and Treasury's section 3 issuance proposal. Filed April 10 to October 13, 2026.
- Covers OCC bank stablecoin engagement, Treasury GENIUS Act state similarity, FDIC payment-stablecoin reserve standards, subsidiary-issuance approvals, resolution submissions, assessments, and disclosure of supervisory information, FinCEN AML/CFT and Permitted Payment Stablecoin Issuer (PPSI) sanctions and customer identification, joint banking AML/CFT, the Board of Governors AML program rule, the SEC draft strategic plan, and the CFTC clearing-organization information collection.

- [Recommendation index](https://tokenization.systems/letters/recommendations/): every recommendation from the letters in one table, by letter, agency and topic, with the status of each as final rules issue.
- [Outcomes so far](https://tokenization.systems/letters/#program-outcomes): one row per proceeding with the comment-period close, the status of the final rule and next dates; also available as an Atom feed at https://tokenization.systems/letters/feed.xml.
- [GENIUS Act rulemaking tracker](https://tokenization.systems/trackers/genius-act/): every implementing rulemaking under the GENIUS Act with publication date, comment deadline, status and sources, including the ones the program did not comment on; also published as JSON at https://tokenization.systems/trackers/genius-act/genius-act.json.

## Notes

- [Notes](https://tokenization.systems/notes/): short, dated notes on rulemaking status, market events and equivalence checks, with an Atom feed at https://tokenization.systems/notes/feed.xml.

## Data and code

- [Data and code](https://tokenization.systems/data/): the letters registry as JSON and CSV, the GENIUS Act tracker as JSON, the compiled letters PDF, and each paper's replication repository, with licences (research content CC BY 4.0).

## Research infrastructure

A cited-research system architecture underlies the program: hundreds of academic sources in a graph-indexed substrate with nine AI-integration patterns for paper drafting, synthesis, revision-impact analysis, cluster discovery, bibliography generation, cross-paper claim synthesis, verbatim quote retrieval, author cluster discovery, and reverse-index lookup. The program's multi-agent research infrastructure, including the Canonical-State Architecture for multi-session coordination, is patent-pending, with filed USPTO applications spanning concurrent repository integrity, evidence and retrieval quality, provenance and artifact coherence, and coordination, fleet governance, and session continuity; the methodology paper documenting the substrate is in development.

## Resume profiles

- [Asset management](https://tokenization.systems/resume/asset-management/): Research, diligence, and decision frameworks for tokenized products and institutional capital allocation.
- [Policy and central banking](https://tokenization.systems/resume/policy/): Research on digital money, stablecoins, settlement, and control-layer infrastructure for policy and market-infrastructure roles.
- [AI governance and infrastructure](https://tokenization.systems/resume/ai-governance-infrastructure/): AI-operator diligence and accountability frameworks (MVEP-AI, CLII-AI).
- [Risk and controls](https://tokenization.systems/resume/risk-controls/): Stress scenarios, finality, and operational risk for tokenized products.
- [Product](https://tokenization.systems/resume/product/): Product strategy for digital-money and tokenized-asset platforms.
- [Stablecoin and payments](https://tokenization.systems/resume/stablecoin-payments/): Gateway routing, reserve mechanics, and payment-stablecoin operator diligence.
